name: mcp__lens_studio__FontSelector
description: Search for fonts by style, mood, or category, and apply fonts to Text/Text3D components. Call with 'query' to search the font database (e.g., 'modern clean sans-serif', 'playful handwriting', 'elegant serif'). Call with 'family' to apply a specific font (e.g., 'Roboto', 'Open Sans', 'Playfair Display'). When 'family' is provided the font is downloaded and imported into the project. It is applied only when there is a target: the Text/Text3D components under 'sceneObjectId', or the text components selected in the editor. With no target, the font is imported without being applied and the result has appliedCount 0. Available categories: sans-serif, serif, display, handwriting, monospace. When searching, the result includes a visual preview image showing how each font renders a pangram.
inputSchema:
exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__lens_studio__FontSelector(args: { category?: "sans-serif" | "serif" | "display" | "handwriting" | "monospace"; family?: string; page?: number; query?: string; sceneObjectId?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

name: mcp__lens_studio__GenerateFast3DAssets
description: Generates 3D assets quickly using AI. Supports creating multiple assets in a single request. Each generation takes about 60 seconds, and multiple assets can be generated in parallel. Use this for quick 3D asset generation when detailed quality is not the primary concern. SCALE NOTE: Generated meshes are uniformly scaled so their longest axis is 1 cm. When imported as a prefab, a default scale transform of 100 is applied on each axis, so the resulting prefab will measure ~100 cm on its longest axis by default. You should adjust the prefab/scene scale after instantiation to match the expected real-world size of the object.


name: mcp__lens_studio__VirtualScene
description:
Batch scene manipulation via declarative instructions. 'read' serializes the scene + assets to a JSON file; 'apply' creates, modifies, and deletes in one call.

## Read
Command 'read' writes project://.virtual-scene.json: scene objects (flat array with parentId) and assets (dot-path props like passInfos.0.baseColor). Use File Read / File Grep on 'project://.virtual-scene.json' to find objects, refs, and property paths.

## Apply
Command 'apply' with an 'instructions' object:

### assets (create)
{ "id": "$temp:sphere", "preset": "SphereMeshPreset", "name": "Sphere" }
{ "id": "$temp:mat", "preset": "UnlitMaterialPreset", "name": "Red", "properties": { "passInfos.0.baseColor": {"x":1,"y":0,"z":0,"w":1} } }

### create (scene objects, optional components)
{ "id": "$temp:obj", "name": "Empty" }
{ "id": "$temp:sun", "name": "Sun", "parentId": "@sceneObject:Solar System", "transform": {"position":[0,0,0],"rotation":[0,0,0],"scale":[8,8,8]}, "components": [{ "type": "RenderMeshVisual", "properties": { "mesh": "$temp:sphere", "mainMaterial": "$temp:mat" } }] }

### modify (prefer over multiple setProperty calls)
Key by a ref; reach component fields with components.TypeName.property dot-paths (copy verbatim from .virtual-scene.json, don't guess). #index selects among same-type components.
{ "@sceneObject:Camera Object": { "transform.position": [0,20,-50], "components.Camera.fov": 45 } }
Add components: "_addComponents": [{ "type": "ScriptComponent", "properties": { "scriptAsset": "@asset:Scripts/Orbit.ts", "speed": 5 } }]
Remove components: "_removeComponents": ["@component:Player/Orbit", "ScriptComponent#0"]
Asset: { "@asset:Red.mat": { "passInfos.0.baseColor": {"x":1,"y":0,"z":0,"w":1} } }

### delete (scene objects and assets only)
["@sceneObject:Old Light", "@asset:Unused.mat"]

## References
@asset:path · @sceneObject:Name (#index for duplicates) · @id:uuid · $temp:label · @component:Object.Type or @component:Object/ScriptClass (resolves to a COMPONENT — see below).

## @component: (wiring component-typed script @inputs)
Use for an @input typed as a component or script class (e.g. @input uiHud: BlowingDandelionUI). @sceneObject: does NOT work there — the engine ignores a SceneObject in a component slot.
- @component:<Object>.<ComponentType>[#index] — engine type, e.g. @component:Hud.Text, @component:Player.ScriptComponent#1
- @component:<Object>/<ScriptClass>[#index] — ScriptComponent by script name (as shown in .virtual-scene.json), e.g. @component:Hud/BlowingDandelionUI
<Object> may be a name (with #index), a UUID, or a same-apply $temp: label. #index disambiguates; zero/ambiguous throws a clear error (never a silent null).
Example: { "@sceneObject:A": { "components.Controller.hud": "@component:B/BlowingDandelionUI" } }

## Property paths
Flat dot-paths — copy verbatim from .virtual-scene.json; don't guess shapes (if the snapshot shows clearColor.color as a vec4, pass a vec4, not clearColor.color.r).

## Script wiring
scriptAsset is set first automatically; other @inputs are deferred and need the TypeScript compiled BEFORE the wiring apply (else a 'recompile' error). Component-typed @inputs: use @component: (above). Array-typed @inputs (e.g. @input items: Item[]) aren't supported here — wire them with scene-graphql.

## Undo
create/modify/delete of objects, components, and properties form one undo group (Cmd+Z reverts atomically). Asset creation writes to disk and is NOT undoable; if an apply partially fails after assets are created, delete the leftover assets in a follow-up apply.
inputSchema:
exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__lens_studio__VirtualScene(args: { command: "read" | "apply"; instructions?: { [key: string]: unknown; }; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

name: mcp__lens_studio__asset_graphql
description:
GraphQL interface for Lens Studio asset mutations and queries: setProperty, createAsset, createNativeAsset, createAssetFromPreset, renameAsset, deleteAsset, duplicateAsset, moveAsset, presets, assetTypes.

ENUM ARG VALUES ARE PASSED WITHOUT QUOTES, in the casing declared by their enum. ValueType is UPPERCASE: NUMBER, STRING, BOOLEAN, ENUM, REFERENCE, VEC2, VEC3, VEC4, MAT3, TRANSFORM, RECT, LAYER_SET_MASK. E.g. setProperty(..., valueType: VEC3). Never pass enum values as strings.

For asset CRUD (rename, move, delete, property edits) and discovery (presets, assetTypes, assets by type), use this tool directly. When asset creation is part of wiring up new scene objects (e.g., material → RenderMeshVisual), prefer VirtualScene 'apply' so creation and wiring happen atomically.

Operations:

ASSET LIFECYCLE:
  createAsset(type: String!, name: String!, destinationPath: String): AssetMutationResult
  createNativeAsset(assetType: String!, name: String!, destinationPath: String): AssetMutationResult
  createAssetFromPreset(presetName: String!, name: String, destinationPath: String): AssetMutationResult
  renameAsset(id: String!, newName: String!): AssetMutationResult
  deleteAsset(id: String!): AssetMutationResult
  duplicateAsset(id: String!, newName: String, destinationPath: String): AssetMutationResult
  moveAsset(id: String!, destinationPath: String!): AssetMutationResult
  setProperty(id: String!, propertyPath: String!, value: JSON, valueType: ValueType!, enumType: String): AssetMutationResult

QUERIES:
  allAssets(typeFilter, nameContains, pathFilter, showPackedContent, limit, offset): [Asset]
  assetsByName(name: String!, exactMatch, typeFilter): [Asset]
  assetCount(typeFilter, nameContains, pathFilter, showPackedContent): Int
  asset(id: String!): Asset                            # single asset by id
  assetByPath(path: String!): Asset                    # single asset by project path
  presets: [AssetPreset]                               # no args; enumerates all asset presets
  preset(presetName: String!): AssetPreset             # NOTE: argument is presetName, not name/type
  assetTypes: [String]                                 # list of valid native asset type strings

PACKAGE ASSETS: allAssets/assetCount exclude package-internal assets (inside .lspkg/.lsc — e.g. SpectaclesInteractionKit/SpectaclesUIKit prefabs) by default, so a query for an installed package prefab returns []. To reach them, pass showPackedContent: true, or use assetsByName(name: ...) which does not filter packed content. Prefab assets have type "ObjectPrefab"; instantiate a found prefab via scene-graphql instantiatePrefab(prefabId: <id>).

All mutations include { success, message, id }; creation mutations also return path.

Property paths use dot notation: e.g. "passInfos.0.baseColor" for nested/array fields.

For setProperty value formats per ValueType, introspect { __type(name:"ValueType") { enumValues { name description } } } — each case documents its expected value shape.
For batching with aliases, JSON-scalar gotchas, full property-path conventions, and recovery patterns, load the scene-construction-skill references.

name: mcp__lens_studio__scene_graphql
description:
GraphQL interface for Lens Studio scene mutations and queries: setProperty, setLocalTransform, createSceneObject, addComponent, instantiatePrefab, createSceneObjectFromPreset, createComponentFromPreset, presets, prefabSceneObjects, and more.

ENUM ARG VALUES ARE PASSED WITHOUT QUOTES, in the casing declared by their enum. ValueType is UPPERCASE: NUMBER, STRING, BOOLEAN, ENUM, REFERENCE, VEC2, VEC3, VEC4, MAT3, TRANSFORM, RECT, LAYER_SET_MASK. ScenePresetType is TitleCase: SceneObject, Component. E.g. presets(type: SceneObject), setProperty(..., valueType: VEC3). Never pass enum values as strings.

For bulk creation or wiring multiple objects/assets together, prefer VirtualScene 'apply'. For broad scene discovery, prefer VirtualScene 'read' + grep on the resulting .virtual-scene.json (cheaper than introspection queries here). Use this tool for targeted mutations on already-known IDs.

Operations (call with already-known IDs, typically from a prior VirtualScene read):

PROPERTY MUTATIONS:
  setProperty(id: String!, propertyPath: String!, value: JSON, valueType: ValueType!, enumType: String): MutationResult
  setEnabled(id: String!, enabled: Boolean!): MutationResult
  setName(id: String!, newName: String!): MutationResult
  setLocalTransform(id: String!, position: JSON, rotation: JSON, scale: JSON): MutationResult
    transform vector args accept {x,y,z}, [x,y,z], or "x, y, z"
  setLayers(id: String!, mask: Int!): MutationResult

HIERARCHY MUTATIONS:
  setParent(id: String!, parentId: String): MutationResult
  createSceneObject(name: String!, parentId: String): MutationResult
  deleteSceneObject(id: String!): MutationResult
  duplicateSceneObject(id: String!, newName: String, parentId: String): MutationResult
  instantiatePrefab(prefabId: String!, parentId: String, name: String): MutationResult

COMPONENT MUTATIONS:
  addComponent(id: String!, componentType: String!): MutationResult
  removeComponent(componentId: String!): MutationResult

PRESET-BASED CREATION:
  createSceneObjectFromPreset(presetName: String!, name: String, parentId: String): MutationResult
  createPrefabFromSceneObject(sceneObjectId: String!, name: String!, destinationPath: String): PrefabMutationResult
  createComponentFromPreset(sceneObjectId: String!, presetName: String!): MutationResult

QUERIES:
  presets(type: ScenePresetType): [ScenePreset]             # type optional; omit to get both SceneObject + Component
  preset(presetName: String!): ScenePreset                  # NOTE: argument is presetName, not name/type
  prefabSceneObjects(prefabId: String!, hasComponent: String, nameContains: String): [SceneObject]

All mutations include { success, message, id }. Some also return parentId, name, type, components, properties, or path — introspect the specific result type for the full shape.

Component types: "ScriptComponent", "ScreenTransform", "Image", "Text", "Camera", "RenderMeshVisual", etc. Shorthand "Script" → "ScriptComponent". For ScriptComponent inputs, use the property name directly (e.g., "speed"), not "inputs.speed".

For setProperty value formats per ValueType, introspect { __type(name:"ValueType") { enumValues { name description } } } — each case documents its expected value shape.
For batching with aliases, JSON-scalar gotchas, full property-path conventions, and recovery patterns, load the scene-construction-skill references.
